{{Quote|Don't they know that painting the ship red only makes it a better target?|Trade Federation gunner [[Jull Dremon]]|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>}}
The '''''Radiant VII''''' was one of many [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class space cruisers]] that were used by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to provide transport to the government's diplomats.

==Characteristics==
The [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser]] ''Radiant VII'' was a 115 [[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long Space Cruiser. It had three [[Dyne 577 radial atomizer engine/Legends|Dyne 577 radial atomizer engines]], and its Long Voltrans tri-arc CD-3.2 hypderdrive engine was a class 2. It had a crew of eight, and a passenger capacity of 16. It was equipped with two 8-person [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]]. The salon pod was capable of being ejected.<ref name="CCS" />

==History==
{{Quote|Captain, look!''"<br />"''Shields up!|The crew of the ''Radiant VII'' moments before its destruction.|audio=WilliamsAndMadakor.flac|<ref name="SWE1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
[[File:Radiant_VII_docked.png|thumb|left|275px|The ''Radiant VII'' docked aboard the ''Saak'ak''.]]
The ''Radiant VII'' was built in the shipyards of [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] above [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. Since [[66 BBY/Legends|66 BBY]] it was in the service of the [[Republic Diplomatic Corps/Legends|Republic Diplomatic Corps]].<ref name="CCS" /> Under [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Maoi Madakor/Legends|Maoi Madakor]], it flew at the [[Battle of Galidraan]].<ref name="JF:OS">''[[Star Wars: Jango Fett: Open Seasons]]''</ref>

Madakor and a new copilot, [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Antidar Williams/Legends|Antidar Williams]], fly the ship on the mission (which would become its last one) that took place<ref name="SWE1" /> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]:<ref name="NEC" /> delivering [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. The Jedi were trying to end the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockade]] that was placed on the planet by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]. However, soon after landing inside the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']], the Trade Federation destroyed ''Radiant VII'' (upon [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]' orders). Both crew members died. This also prevented an easier escape for Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi. The two Jedi were then forced to escape from the ''Saak'ak.''<ref name="SWE1" /> On their way through the vessel's hangar bay, Jinn and Kenobi took cover behind the ''Radiant VII's'' wreckage while they disabled a laser turret.<ref name="SW:OW">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Radiant VII'' first appeared in [[1999]] with [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].

The early designs of the ''Radiant VII'' had a smooth, "[[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]-look" to it. After several iterations, [[George Lucas]] and [[Doug Chiang]] decided that the cruiser should have a strong visual link to the [[original trilogy]]. With that direction, Chiang and the Art Department devised a ship with a more rectilinear profile that echoed the design of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'''s]] [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']]. One of the last additions to the cruiser was the small antenna array that rests above the cockpit. Lucas felt that the ship needed "a little extra something" to guide the audience's eyes to that section of the ship.

The vessel's destruction in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|adaptation]] differs slightly from the the movie. In the movie, the ''Radiant VII'' was destroyed before the Jedi leave the conference room, but in the game, it explodes after Kenobi escaped the conference room and reached the hangar bay.

The vessel was also reimagined in LEGO form in [[2005]] for the opening cutscene of ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'', which was also included in the [[2007]] [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|compilation re-release]].
